card: This pull request avoids running the second coin selection pass for Avoid Partial Spends (APS) when the wallet's initial coin selection does not leave any partial spends. Currently, APS runs unconditionally whenever enabled by fee settings, wasting computation, potentially degrading selection efficiency, and overreporting APS usage in USDT tracepoints (fixing issue #25150). The change calculates available versus selected UTXO counts per scriptPubKey and only attempts APS if a partial spend actually occurred.
changed_since_previous: Diff provided for the first time; implementation inspects available and preset coins per scriptPubKey in CreateTransactionInternal and exposes has_partial_spend to CreateTransaction.
evidence: Closes issue #25150: 'Coin Selection tracepoint overreports use of APS'

PR description: 'APS currently runs unconditionally, even when the first selection has no partial spend. Running APS unnecessarily wastes computation and can produce a worse result when there was nothing to fix.'
problem: Bitcoin Core's wallet unconditionally runs a second coin selection pass with Avoid Partial Spends enabled if fees allow it, even when no scriptPubKey was partially spent in the first pass. This wastes CPU cycles during transaction creation, can lead to worse coin selection results, and causes USDT tracepoints to report APS execution when APS had no effect.

risk.why: A flaw in partial spend accounting could incorrectly skip APS when it should run or alter coin selection behavior during transaction creation.

summary: Skips the Avoid Partial Spends (APS) coin selection pass when the initial selection already leaves no partially spent scriptPubKeys. Counts available versus selected UTXOs per scriptPubKey during transaction creation to set a new has_partial_spend flag on CreatedTransactionResult. Updates USDT coin selection tracepoint functional tests to construct multi-UTXO scenarios where partial spends actually occur.
